metadata.note: The Washington and Old Dominion (W&OD) and its predecessors, Northern Virginia: the electric Great Falls and Old Dominion (Georgetown - Great Falls, 1906-1911); the W&OD Railway / Railroad 1912-1951 (Bluemont Division Rosslyn - Purcellville - Bluemont, Great Falls Division, Alexandria branch, Georgetown terminal over the Aqueduct Bridge; passenger gap Apr 1941 - Mar 1943; last passenger train 31 May 1951); and the steam road it leased - Alexandria, Loudoun & Hampshire 1859-1861, Washington & Ohio and its renamings 1866-1888, Richmond & Danville 1888-1893 and Southern Railway Bluemont Branch 1894-1912. Research report: research/branches/washington_and_old_dominion_railway.txt.
sources: Harwood, Rails to the Blue Ridge (3rd ed.), full text -- https://web.archive.org/web/20170928181826/http://www.scc.virginia.gov/docketsearch/DOCS/198p01!.PDF
Fowler, Maryland, Virginia & West Virginia Interurban Railways, lines 205-207 -- https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/marylandvirginiaandwvinterurbanrlys.pdf
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (Overpass, maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-26): old_railway_operator=W&OD ways (W&OD Railroad Regional Park trail; abandoned/razed Washington and Old Dominion Railroad ways; Mount Jefferson trail), Bluemont Junction Trail, Custis Trail, I-66 (Custis Memorial Parkway), Old Dominion Drive (VA 309 / SR 738) and railway=abandoned "Old Dominion Drive" ways
metadata.operator_split: Features split at every change of operator (Rule 4), sharing geometry: AL&H 1859-61 and Washington & Ohio 1866-88 (one road, one colour) -> Richmond & Danville 1888-93 -> Southern Railway 1894-1912 -> W&OD 1912-1951. GF&OD 1906-1911 -> W&OD 1912. The 16 Apr 1936 W&OD Railway -> W&OD Railroad reorganisation and the 1945 purchase of the line from the Southern are NOT splits (same operator; title change only). Southern Railway colour pulled programmatically from the existing Southern Railway features.
metadata.mode_decisions: interurban for the W&OD electric era 1912-1941 and the GF&OD (Rule 7: electric line linking Washington with Loudoun County towns). commuter_rail for 1943-1951 (gas-electric and diesel motor cars, wires gone - not an electric interurban) and for the 1912-1932 Alexandria branch shuttle (unelectrified 7-mile feeder shuttle meeting the electric trains at Bluemont Junction; traction after c.1919 unresolved). intercity_rail for the pre-1912 steam roads.
not_yet_sourced: Last pre-war passenger day: 12 Apr 1941 (Evening Star) vs 23 Apr 1941 (Harwood p.81); year firm.
Purcellville - Bluemont end month Feb (Wikipedia) vs Mar 1939 (Harwood); primary confirmation only to Nov 1938.
Alexandria branch passenger end 1932 (Harwood) vs 1934 (Wikipedia citing Williams); drawn to 1932.
Alexandria branch traction after c.1919 (steam vs electric-division cars on an unwired branch).
Leesburg - Purcellville riders re-admitted late 1943 (Harwood) vs Feb 1944 (Fairfax Herald); drawn from 1944.
GF&OD -> W&OD handover month (1911 incorporation vs 1912 divisional reorganisation).
AL&H last civilian train in 1861 undated; 1861 end is approximate.
Pre-1912 dates from Wikipedia and a partly illegible Harwood chronology page; W&W / WO&W takeover dates and the 1900 Bluemont extension not checked against a primary source.

properties.line: Washington and Old Dominion: Bluemont Division
properties.speed_source: Harwood pp.51, 89: about 20 mph (32 km/h) average, Washington - Bluemont 2 - 2.5 h (1913) and Rosslyn - Purcellville 45 mi in 2 h 20 (1944-51), measured from timetables in the company history. Not re-checked against a timetable.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 44.7 mi against 44.6 mi documented (Fowler line 205, Rosslyn - Purcellville mileposts). Rosslyn - Thrifton (1.6 mi) is APPROXIMATED: the right-of-way lies under I-66 (Custis Memorial Parkway) and is drawn on the I-66 carriageway, joined to a hand-pinned Rosslyn by a 0.3 mi straight line and to Thrifton junction by a 0.3 mi straight line. Thrifton - Bluemont Junction (the 1912 connecting line, 2.8 mi) is APPROXIMATED from Thrifton to Ballston: a 0.6 mi straight line along I-66 from Thrifton, then the Custis Trail beside I-66 (both built on the W&OD right-of-way), then a 0.4 mi straight line from the Custis Trail to the north-east end of the Bluemont Junction Trail at Ballston; Ballston - Bluemont Junction (1.2 mi) is traced on the Bluemont Junction Trail (the connector's own grade). Bluemont Junction - Purcellville is traced on the W&OD Railroad Regional Park trail / W&OD-tagged OSM ways throughout (0.3 mi near Purcellville on the OpenHistoricalMap Washington & Ohio way); no straight-line leg west of Bluemont Junction. LATER ALIGNMENT: Rosslyn is drawn at one point for 1912-1941; the 1923 Rosslyn terminal and the post-1939 makeshift platform at the car shop a block west are not distinguished. Bluemont Junction - Purcellville is the rail-trail, i.e. the line as abandoned in 1968.

segments.note: W&OD Railway took over all service on the leased Southern Bluemont Branch on 1 Jul 1912 (Harwood p.50); for the first months rented Southern steam trains ran west of Bluemont Junction, electric cars to Leesburg from 6 Oct 1912 and to Bluemont by end-Dec 1912 (Harwood p.51). Initially 14 trains each way (4 Herndon, 5 Leesburg, 5 Bluemont) plus 12 Georgetown - Bluemont Jct locals; cut to 10 by end-1913 (Harwood p.51). The Washington terminal was Georgetown until Dec 1923 (feature wod-georgetown-rosslyn). headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.
sources: Segment-level: start date and train counts from Harwood, Rails to the Blue Ridge (3rd ed.), pp.50-51.

segments.note: About 10 trains each way from end-1913, including the "Loudoun Limited" with parlor car (dropped 1932) (Harwood pp.51, 76). Rosslyn became the Washington terminal in Dec 1923. W&OD Railway in receivership from 1932. headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.

1932: the short-haul Rosslyn - Bluemont Junction locals were cut (Harwood p.76) - through trains continued over that piece. About 6 round trips in the 1930s (Harwood p.76). On 16 Apr 1936 the W&OD Railway's operations passed to the new Washington and Old Dominion Railroad (Davis Elkins) - a receivership reorganisation under the same management and name, not an operator change (Harwood p.79). headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.

From Mar 1939 trains ended at Purcellville: 2 to Purcellville + 2 to Leesburg; by Oct 1940 only 2 Purcellville round trips (Harwood p.80). All passenger service ended in April 1941 - the Evening Star of 12 Apr 1941 (p.22) reports the last passenger trip that day, before the State Corporation Commission's midnight deadline, while Harwood p.81 has the last train reach Rosslyn on 23 Apr 1941 after three successive delays (conflict on the day recorded; the year is firm). Mail-express car 44 then ran the old schedule with NO passengers until Mar 1943 - not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.
sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.80-81; Evening Star 12 Apr 1941 p.22.

Georgetown (36th & M Sts) - Rosslyn (0.4 mi drawn vs 0.3 mi Fowler) is a HAND-DRAWN STRAIGHT LINE in three legs over the site of the Aqueduct Bridge (removed 1933), just upstream of Key Bridge; the bridge alignment and the Georgetown terminal position are approximated from the street grid, not traced.

segments.note: The W&OD's Washington terminal at 36th & M Sts, Georgetown, reached over the Aqueduct Bridge; both divisions' cars started here (inherited from the GF&OD, feature gfod-georgetown-great-falls). Key Bridge opened Jan 1923, but the W&OD kept running over the Aqueduct Bridge for most of 1923; the new Rosslyn terminal opened in December and the bridge operation ceased (Harwood p.51). This was the W&OD's only mileage in DC. Headway is an estimate for Great Falls and Bluemont cars combined.
sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.50-51 for the 1912 start and the Dec 1923 end. (1923 Evening Star articles confirming the bridge operation were found by the researcher but their page IDs were not kept.)

Purcellville - Round Hill (3.0 mi) is traced on three short W&OD-tagged OSM ways and, between them (1.5 mi), the OpenHistoricalMap "Washington & Ohio Railroad" way -200509739 (Google My Maps-derived, precision unchecked); Round Hill - Bluemont (3.6 mi) on W&OD-tagged OSM way 169913850, plus a 0.2 mi approximated straight line to a hand-pinned Bluemont terminal where the mapped grade ends.  The trace is 0.5 mi short: the Bluemont terminal is pinned where the mapped grade ends, and the OHM section is generalised.

segments.note: W&OD took over from the Southern on 1 Jul 1912; electric cars to Bluemont from end-Dec 1912 (Harwood pp.50-51). 5 of the initial 14 daily trains each way ran through to Bluemont, the summer-excursion terminus at the foot of the Blue Ridge (Harwood p.51). headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.

Fewer trains through the 1930s (about 6 round trips on the division, Harwood p.76). ICC abandonment application Aug 1938; the ICC examiner's report (Evening Star 10 Nov 1938 p.24) notes protests "as passenger and freight service is available over the route at present" - primary evidence of passengers in Nov 1938. "In March 1939 W&OD trains ended their runs at Purcellville" (Harwood p.80); Wikipedia says February 1939 - month conflict recorded, year 1939 from two secondary accounts. Rails and wire went to the Southern as salvage. headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.
sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.79-80 (Mar 1939 end); Evening Star 10 Nov 1938 p.24 (passengers carried Nov 1938).

Rosslyn - Thrifton (1.6 mi) is APPROXIMATED: the right-of-way lies under I-66 (Custis Memorial Parkway) and is drawn on the I-66 carriageway, joined to a hand-pinned Rosslyn by a 0.3 mi straight line and to Thrifton junction by a 0.3 mi straight line. segments.note: Wartime restart after the Apr 1941 - Mar 1943 freight/mail-only gap: passenger service resumed 22 Mar 1943 with a single commuter round trip Rosslyn - Leesburg (Harwood p.85 and chronology, PDF p.113 of the archived scan; Blue Ridge Herald 18 Mar 1943 via Wikipedia). Riders were re-admitted on the two Rosslyn - Purcellville mail-express runs later in 1943 / Feb 1944, which also cross this stretch. The Leesburg commuter trip was dropped Jun 1950 (Harwood p.90); the Purcellville runs continued until the last passenger train, car 45, on 31 May 1951 (Harwood pp.90-91; Evening Star 1 Jun 1951 p.8). Not electric - the wires were gone: leased ex-PRR Budd gas-electric train, then gas-electric cars 45 (ex-NYC), 46 (ex-GM&O), 52 (ex-NYC RPO combine) and diesel-hauled cars, so mode commuter_rail rather than interurban. No tickets sold; Rosslyn "station" was the car-shop overhang. Headway is an estimate (about 3 trains each way at best, 2 after Jun 1950).
sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.85-91 and chronology (PDF p.113 - re-check printed folio); Evening Star 1 Jun 1951 p.8.

segments.note: Mail-express car 44 kept running Rosslyn - Purcellville through 1941-43 with no riders (not drawn). Riders were re-admitted "later in 1943" when GM&O car 46 arrived (Harwood p.88), or in Feb 1944 (Fairfax Herald 4 Feb 1944, "W.&O.D. Service is increased", via Wikipedia) - the bracket collapses to 1944. Car 52 normally worked the four Purcellville trains, carrying mail and express with the passengers (1944 timetable, Harwood p.92). Ended with the last passenger train on 31 May 1951 (Evening Star 1 Jun 1951 p.8), with the loss of the Post Office mail contract. Gas-electric motor cars, so commuter_rail. Headway estimate: 2 trains each way.
sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.88-92; Wikipedia citing Fairfax Herald 4 Feb 1944; Evening Star 1 Jun 1951 p.8.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 12.0 mi against 12.1 mi documented (Fowler line 207, MP 1.7 - 13.8 from Rosslyn). Thrifton - Great Falls Park: Thrifton - the GF&OD grade at Glebe Rd (1.2 mi) is an APPROXIMATED STRAIGHT LINE through Cherrydale (the grade there is lost; Thrifton is placed at the east end of a surviving street stub named Old Dominion Drive, which fits Fowler's MP 1.7 from Rosslyn); Glebe Rd - Great Falls Park is traced on Old Dominion Drive (VA 309 / SR 738) and four OSM railway=abandoned ways named "Old Dominion Drive" in Arlington. LATER ALIGNMENT: Old Dominion Drive is the road built on the right-of-way after the rails were pulled in 1935, so the drawn line is the road's centreline; how closely the road keeps to the 1906-1934 grade was not checked, and the Great Falls terminal is hand-pinned near the park entrance.

segments.note: The former Great Falls and Old Dominion line became the W&OD's Great Falls Division in 1912 (Harwood p.50). Busiest W&OD segment: 128+ daily trains in 1916 (Harwood p.77). Double track from 1908. Served the company-built Great Falls amusement park. Cars ran through from Georgetown (to 1923) or Rosslyn over the Bluemont Division track to Thrifton. Headway estimate from the 1916 train count.

Down to 28 daily trains by 1932, track progressively singled 1932-34 (Harwood p.77). "The entire Great Falls Division west of the Thrifton junction was shut down on June 8, 1934" (Harwood p.77; Evening Star 12 Apr 1941 retrospective: "The Great Falls line was dropped in 1934"). Passenger to the day it closed; rails pulled mid-1935 and the right-of-way became Old Dominion Drive. Headway estimate from the 1932 count.
sources: Segment-level: Harwood p.77; Evening Star 12 Apr 1941 p.22.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 7.0 mi against 7.1 mi documented (Fowler line 206) / 7.6 mi (Harwood p.29, PDF page). Alexandria (Fairfax St) - Alexandria Junction (1.4 mi) is traced on the OpenHistoricalMap "Washington & Ohio Railroad" ways (-202019757, -202019758; a Google My Maps-derived source, precision unchecked) and the OSM W&OD-tagged Mount Jefferson trail; the Fairfax St terminal is hand-pinned at Princess/Fairfax Sts. Alexandria Junction - Shirlington - Bluemont Junction (5.6 mi) is traced on W&OD-tagged ways and the W&OD trail along Four Mile Run (0.2 mi on the Four Mile Run Trail).  LATER ALIGNMENT: the Four Mile Run section is the line as abandoned in the 1960s (now the W&OD trail and Mount Jefferson trail); the W&OD's cars were moved over Southern track east of the Potomac Yard trestle to the old AL&H depots, and that street-running approach is drawn on the OHM AL&H/W&O alignment.

segments.note: W&OD shuttles Alexandria (old AL&H depot, Princess/Fairfax Sts) - Bluemont Junction, meeting the electric trains: 6 each way in 1912, 5 by end-1913 (Harwood pp.48-51). The branch was UNELECTRIFIED (Harwood p.48; Fowler: "Unelectrified") and the shuttles were steam 2-8-0 hauled to c.1919; Harwood p.50 says electric-division cars later worked them, unexplained on an unwired branch. Mode is commuter_rail: a short steam (later possibly hauled-car) feeder shuttle, not an electric interurban (Rule 7 does not fit an unwired branch) and not a through intercity train. "In 1932 he cut off all the short-haul trains between Rosslyn, Bluemont Junction, and Alexandria. Alexandria ... became its first 'freight service only' city" (Harwood p.76). CONFLICT: Wikipedia, citing Williams p.74, says the receivers ended Bluemont Junction - Alexandria passenger service in 1934; drawn to the earlier 1932. Freight continued into the 1960s (not drawn). headway_min is an estimate derived from the train counts quoted, not a timetable interval.
sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.48-51, 76 (1932 end); conflicting 1934 end in Wikipedia citing Williams p.74.

Elkins): trial run to Difficult Run Mar 1906, first scheduled car Georgetown (36th & M Sts) - Great Falls 3 Jul 1906, over the Aqueduct Bridge and through Rosslyn and Thrifton; double-tracked 1908. In 1911 the same owners incorporated the Washington and Old Dominion Railway, and in 1912 the line became its Great Falls Division (features wod-georgetown-rosslyn, wod-bluemont-division for Rosslyn - Thrifton, wod-great-falls-division) - ended at 1911 so the two companies do not overlap; the handover month is not established. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: GF&OD Wikipedia article (citing Harwood pp.39-46) for the 1906 opening; Harwood pp.46-50 for the 1911/12 change of company.

segments.note: The Alexandria, Loudoun & Hampshire (chartered 1853) opened from Alexandria to Vienna in Aug 1859 (Harwood chronology, PDF p.113; Wikipedia). Ran to 1861, when the line was seized by Union forces and the Confederates removed its locomotives (Harwood PDF p.132; Wikipedia). The 1861 end is APPROXIMATE - no source dates the last civilian train - and Civil War military operation 1861-65 is not drawn. Headway is an estimate (one or two trains a day).
sources: Segment-level: Harwood chronology (PDF p.113, partly illegible) and Wikipedia for the 1859 opening; end 1861 approximate, no segment-level source for the last civilian train.

segments.note: Civilian service resumed to Herndon on 9 Jan 1866 (Wikipedia). Operated after the war by the AL&H (to 1870), renamed Washington & Ohio 1870, reorganised as Washington & Western 1882 and Washington, Ohio & Western 1883 - one road under successive names, drawn as one company and one colour (Rule 4). Leased to the Richmond & Danville 1886, which operated the trains from 1888 (features rd-*). Trains terminated in Alexandria; through service to Washington before 1888 is not established. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Southern Railway (formed 1894 from the R&D) ran Washington - Round Hill, and from 1900 Bluemont (feature southern-round-hill-bluemont): 4-6 daily trips each way plus summer weekend nonstop excursions (Harwood pp.8-9). Washington terminal PRR 6th & B St station, Union Station from c.1907-08. A GE gas-electric car (No. 1) made a Washington - Leesburg round trip from 1911 (Harwood PDF p.132). The W&OD took over all service on 1 Jul 1912 under lease (Southern kept ownership to 1945); the W&OD features take over from 1912. Headway is an estimate from the trip count.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia and Harwood pp.8-9, 46, 50 for the 1894 start, train counts and the 30 Jun 1912 end.

Mode commuter_rail, as for the W&OD shuttle it became: a short local feeder, not a through train. [OPEN start] 1908 is the FIRST CONFIRMED year ("by 1908"), not a known start: the shuttle probably ran earlier, under the R&D and the Southern, but no source dates it. sources: Segment-level: Harwood pp.8-9 states the shuttle by 1908; earlier years unconfirmed.
